fixes.description: SearchAsync queued only the ranked maxCandidates for human review - review routing was computed from the score-sorted list AFTER Take(maxCandidates) was applied, so an above-threshold candidate crowded out of the returned top-N (e.g. a caller requesting only the single best match while several candidates score above the duplicate threshold) never reached the review queue at all, violating AC03's requirement that every possible duplicate route to human review.
fixes.fix: FingerprintSearchService.SearchAsync now computes review routing (RaiseOrAugmentReviewAsync) from the full, uncapped scored set, before Take(maxCandidates) is applied to the RETURNED ranked list. AC01's cap on what the caller sees and AC03's routing of every possible duplicate to review are now independent concerns that can legitimately differ in size.
fixes.regression_tests: tests/features/bio-bio-006/FingerprintSearchServiceTests.cs::AC03_every_above_threshold_candidate_routes_to_review_even_when_crowded_out_of_the_capped_ranked_list - three candidates all score above the duplicate threshold, maxCandidates: 1 requested; asserts the returned ranked list has exactly one entry while all three still appear as PendingReview entries in the review queue.

fixes.description: AC03 review routing was not concurrency-safe. RaiseOrAugmentReviewAsync's read-check-write (read the entry, then create or replace) was not atomic: two simultaneous searches that both first observed the SAME (subject, candidate) pair as a new possible duplicate both read null, and both attempted to create an entry. The repository's own uniqueness check correctly rejected the second write, but nothing in the service converged the two legitimate concurrent callers onto the one successfully-raised entry, so one received an unhandled already_exists exception instead.
fixes.fix: Added Domain/FingerprintDuplicateReviewLockRegistry.cs, the same per-pair SemaphoreSlim shape BIO-IDN-005's own DuplicateCandidateLockRegistry uses for its structurally identical aggregate. FingerprintSearchService now acquires this lock across the whole read-check-write sequence in both RaiseOrAugmentReviewAsync and DecideAsync (the latter's own read-check(version)-write has the identical race shape). Registered as a Singleton in BioBio006Module. Different pairs still proceed fully in parallel - only operations on the same pair are serialized.
fixes.regression_tests: tests/features/bio-bio-006/FingerprintDuplicateReviewLockRegistryTests.cs - direct, deterministic proof that a second acquire for the same pair waits until the first is released, and that acquiring a different pair never waits on an unrelated pair's lock. tests/features/bio-bio-006/FingerprintSearchServiceTests.cs::AC03_two_simultaneous_searches_raising_the_same_new_pair_both_converge_without_throwing - two Task.Run-scheduled concurrent SearchAsync calls for the same new pair, asserting both complete without throwing and converge on exactly one PendingReview entry.

summary: Implements BIO-BIO-006 (1:N fingerprint search for duplicate detection/identification, without automatic identity merge), built directly on BIO-BIO-001's provider-neutral biometric contracts (IFingerprintProvider/IBiometricMatcher/BiometricTemplate). AC01: FingerprintSearchService.SearchAsync compares a live probe against every OTHER identity in this feature's own IFingerprintGalleryStore (a searchable 'gallery', deliberately separate from BIO-BIO-001's own per-identity IBiometricTemplateStore, which cannot enumerate a tenant's population - modifying that interface would be out of this story's write scope), returns FingerprintSearchCandidate entries ordered by score descending and capped at the caller-requested maxCandidates. AC02: a genuinely distinct permission key (FingerprintSearchService.SearchPermissionKey = 'biometric.fingerprint_search_1n') is checked via the narrow IBiometricSearchPermissionGateway (real adapter wraps BIO-IDN-006's already-registered PermissionService.ActorHasPermissionAsync) BEFORE the gallery is even read; BIO-BIO-004's own 1:1 verification enforces no permission today (a pre-existing, out-of-scope-to-retrofit decision from that story), so 'distinguishing' 1:N from 1:1 is satisfied by this key being independently grantable, never implied by any other grant. AC03 (after both round-2/round-3 fixes): EVERY candidate meeting IFingerprintDuplicateThresholdPolicy's tenant-resolved threshold is raised/augmented onto this feature's own FingerprintDuplicateReviewEntry queue, independent of AC01's own maxCandidates cap on the returned ranked list, and the raise/augment/decide sequence is now serialized per pair via FingerprintDuplicateReviewLockRegistry so concurrent observers of the same duplicate converge instead of racing - mirroring BIO-IDN-005's own DuplicateCandidate discipline (ordered-pair natural key, signals/score accumulate, a decided pair is never silently reopened by a later search, per-pair locking). BIO-IDN-005 itself anticipates a future biometric-sourced duplicate signal via its own DuplicateSignalSource.Biometric enum member, but the only method that could raise one (DuplicateReviewService.RaiseOrAugmentAsync) is private with no public entry point any ProjectReference could reach, so this story owns its own self-contained review queue instead, deliberately vocabulary-matched to BIO-IDN-005's own for a future migration path. AC04: this project has zero ProjectReference to BIO-IDN-001 anywhere, so it structurally cannot call PersonService to merge/archive/delete anything; FingerprintDuplicateReviewStatus has no Merged member. AC05: IFingerprintGalleryStore/IFingerprintDuplicateReviewRepository are both keyed by tenant with cross-tenant lookups returning null/empty (no enumeration oracle, ADR-0001 §1.5), and SearchAsync accepts no parameter that could widen a search beyond the resolved tenant. BIO-BIO-002 (the approved story's own declared dependency) is documented as an intentional non-dependency, the identical situation BIO-BIO-004 already established for the same reason (no queryable-by-identity capability exists in that story's own internal, Singleton-registered repository) - the gallery is instead populated via an explicit IndexAsync registration step. Repository/gallery-store/lock-registry/service are all internal or Singleton-registered as appropriate, gated by an explicit InternalsVisibleTo seam (BIO-IDN-001-QA-01 governance shape, mirrored from every prior BIO-BIO story).
